sources.title: Executive summary: DOJ review of the 2006–2008 Epstein investigation
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Office of Professional Responsibility
sources.notes: Primary official review. Printed pages i–iii cover the investigation, September 24, 2007 agreement and June 30, 2008 plea; printed page v covers dismissal of the 2019 indictment. PDF page numbers include a cover.

sources.title: DOJ findings on prosecutors' handling of the Epstein investigation
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice
sources.notes: OPR found poor judgment and inadequate treatment of victims, but did not find professional misconduct by DOJ attorneys.

sources.title: Jeffrey Epstein charged with sex trafficking of minors
sources.publisher: U.S. Attorney's Office, Southern District of New York
sources.notes: United States v. Epstein, 1:19-cr-00490 (RMB), indictment Dkt. 2. An indictment states allegations; the defendant died before trial.

sources.title: United States v. Jeffrey Epstein, 19 Cr. 490 (RMB)
sources.publisher: U.S. Attorney's Office, Southern District of New York
sources.notes: Official case information and indictment-dismissal history.

sources.title: Ghislaine Maxwell sentenced to 20 years
sources.publisher: U.S. Attorney's Office, Southern District of New York
sources.notes: United States v. Maxwell, 1:20-cr-00330. Records the December 29, 2021 jury verdict and June 28, 2022 sentence.

sources.title: Maxwell v. United States: order denying post-conviction relief
sources.publisher: U.S. District Court, SDNY; document reproduced by Justia
sources.notes: 25 Civ. 10468 (PAE), Dkt. 10; related criminal case 20 Cr. 330. Primary judicial opinion, not a news summary. Pages 1–7 summarize conviction, sentence, appeal and October 6, 2025 denial of certiorari; final order denies the section 2255 petition.

sources.title: Report concerning Jeffrey Epstein's interactions with MIT
sources.publisher: Goodwin Procter LLP, commissioned by MIT
sources.notes: Institution-commissioned review. Printed pp. 7–11: donations, Minsky, Bach, Lloyd and Oxman; pp. 11–18: donor cultivation; p. 47: July 19, 2013 meeting. The report corrects an earlier attendee list for October 23, 2013 in footnote 45; do not use the superseded list.

sources.title: MIT releases fact-finding results on engagements with Epstein
sources.publisher: Massachusetts Institute of Technology
sources.notes: MIT's summary of its commissioned investigation; distinguish the institution's findings from a criminal judgment.

sources.title: MIT donates $850,000 to organizations supporting survivors
sources.publisher: Massachusetts Institute of Technology
sources.notes: The amount equals the donations the MIT review attributed to Epstein.

sources.title: Report regarding Jeffrey Epstein's connections to Harvard
sources.publisher: Harvard University
sources.notes: University review and General Counsel's detailed cover letter: $9,179,000 in gifts during 1998–2007; $6.5 million for PED in 2003; 2005 visiting fellowship; more than 40 PED office visits during 2010–2018. The introductory letter uses a rounded total and broader date wording; the detailed findings provide the precise amount and gift years.

sources.title: NYDFS consent order with Deutsche Bank
sources.publisher: New York State Department of Financial Services
sources.notes: Primary consent order. Paragraph 11: relationship August 2013–December 2018. Paragraph 24: August 19, 2013 accounts for Southern Trust Company and Southern Financial. Findings of banking compliance failures, not criminal judgments against every transaction recipient.

sources.title: NYDFS announces $150 million Deutsche Bank penalty
sources.publisher: New York State Department of Financial Services
sources.notes: Penalty covers three sets of banking relationships: Epstein, Danske Estonia and FBME. Do not describe the full $150 million as an Epstein-only penalty.

sources.title: JPMorgan Chase registration document: Epstein litigation
sources.publisher: JPMorgan Chase & Co.
sources.notes: PDF page 65, section 'Jeffrey Epstein Litigation': banking through 2013, $290 million settlement, June 2023 preliminary approval and November 2023 final approval. Issuer disclosure.

sources.title: USVI government announces $75 million JPMorgan settlement
sources.publisher: Government of the United States Virgin Islands
sources.notes: Government of the USVI v. JPMorgan Chase Bank, 1:22-cv-10904 (SDNY). A civil settlement; government's characterization of the agreement.

sources.title: JPMorgan to pay $75 million to settle USVI claims
sources.publisher: Associated Press
sources.notes: Independent reporting on the settlement and separate confidential agreement between JPMorgan and former executive Jes Staley. Settlement is not a criminal conviction.

sources.title: Dechert report on Leon Black, Epstein and Apollo
sources.publisher: Dechert LLP for Apollo's Conflicts Committee; filed with SEC
sources.notes: Apollo January 25, 2021 Form 8-K, Exhibit 99.1. Printed pp. 3–4: services and $158 million; p. 4: 263,257 Apollo IPO shares; pp. 5–6: Black Family Foundation director 1997–2007. A company-commissioned investigation, not a judicial ruling or regulator exoneration.

sources.title: DOJ Inspector General findings on Epstein's detention and death
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Office of the Inspector General
sources.notes: Official report announcement, pp. 1–2: serious prison failures, falsified records and recording-system deficiencies; no evidence contradicting FBI determination of no criminal act causing the death; medical examiner ruled suicide.

sources.title: DOJ announces first-phase release of Epstein records
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice
sources.notes: Includes categories such as flight logs and a redacted contact book; neither category by itself establishes wrongdoing.

sources.title: Maxwell grand-jury disclosure opinion and order
sources.publisher: U.S. District Court, Southern District of New York
sources.notes: 20 Cr. 330 (PAE), p. 7 reproduces the July 2025 DOJ/FBI memorandum's findings. Its grand-jury disclosure ruling predates the Epstein Files Transparency Act and later December 2025 order.

sources.title: DOJ announces nearly 3.5 million released pages
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice
sources.notes: DOJ's production count and stated methodology, updated February 1. Explicitly warns that the released corpus includes material submitted by the public that may be false. This source does not authenticate every released document's assertions.

sources.title: DOJ Epstein Library and disclosure index
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice
sources.notes: Displayed last-updated date September 11, 2026. The site warns of search limitations and potential inadvertent sensitive disclosures. Only selected records were reviewed for this dataset.

entities.name: Ghislaine Maxwell

entities.name: Alexander Acosta

entities.name: U.S. Department of Justice

entities.name: Federal Bureau of Investigation
entities.summary: Federal investigative agency involved in the Epstein and Maxwell investigations.

entities.name: Federal Bureau of Prisons
entities.summary: Federal detention agency whose custody and supervision of Epstein were examined by the DOJ Inspector General.

entities.name: Massachusetts Institute of Technology
entities.summary: Its 2020 commissioned review documented Epstein donations and visits and failures in handling the association.

entities.name: MIT Media Lab
entities.summary: MIT research laboratory that received Epstein donations documented in the institute's 2020 review.

entities.name: Joi Ito

entities.name: Marvin Minsky

entities.name: Joscha Bach

entities.name: Seth Lloyd
entities.summary: MIT professor whose research received Epstein donations documented by MIT's review.

entities.name: Reid Hoffman
entities.summary: Technology investor listed in MIT's review as a participant in a July 19, 2013 campus meeting with Epstein.

entities.name: Neil Gershenfeld
entities.summary: MIT professor listed as a participant in a July 19, 2013 campus meeting in MIT's Epstein review.

entities.name: Megan Smith

entities.name: Harvard University

entities.name: Harvard Program for Evolutionary Dynamics

entities.name: Martin Nowak

entities.summary: Bank that maintained Epstein-related accounts from 2013 to 2018 and entered a 2020 NYDFS consent order over compliance failures.

entities.name: New York State Department of Financial Services
entities.summary: Banking regulator that issued the 2020 Deutsche Bank consent order.

entities.name: JPMorgan Chase
entities.summary: Bank that provided Epstein services through 2013 and later settled related civil litigation.

entities.name: Government of the U.S. Virgin Islands

entities.name: Leon Black
entities.summary: Apollo co-founder who personally retained Epstein for financial advice, as described in a company-commissioned review.

entities.name: Apollo Global Management

entities.name: Black Family Foundation
entities.summary: Leon Black's family philanthropic foundation; the Dechert review dates Epstein's directorship to 1997–2007.

events.title: Epstein joins Black Family Foundation board
events.summary: The Dechert review dates Epstein's appointment as an initial foundation director to 1997 and his resignation to mid-2007.
events.limitations: Company-commissioned review, printed pp. 5–6. It says later tax filings mistakenly continued to list him.

events.title: Harvard donation period begins
events.summary: Harvard's review counts $9,179,000 in gifts during 1998–2007.
events.limitations: Start of a date range. Harvard says it accepted no Epstein gifts after his 2008 conviction.

events.title: MIT gift supports Minsky's research
events.summary: MIT documented a $100,000 Epstein-funded gift for Marvin Minsky's research and an off-campus AI conference they organized that year.
events.limitations: Printed p. 9. Research funding and conference organization establish those specific connections only.

events.title: Epstein funds Harvard evolutionary-dynamics program
events.summary: A $6.5 million gift helped create Harvard's Program for Evolutionary Dynamics.
events.limitations: University review; the gift preceded the 2008 conviction.

events.title: Palm Beach investigation begins
events.summary: Palm Beach police began investigating Epstein following a report involving a minor.
events.limitations: OPR summary, printed p. i. Victim-identifying details are omitted.

events.title: Harvard grants a visiting fellowship
events.summary: Harvard appointed Epstein a visiting fellow. Its later review found that he lacked the customary academic qualifications.
events.limitations: A visiting fellowship was not a faculty appointment.

events.title: Federal non-prosecution agreement signed
events.summary: Southern District of Florida prosecutors agreed to forgo federal prosecution under an agreement requiring a state plea, incarceration and other conditions.
events.limitations: OPR summary, printed pp. i–ii. The agreement's scope later became a disputed legal issue.

events.title: Epstein pleads guilty in Florida
events.summary: Epstein pleaded guilty to felony solicitation of prostitution and procurement of minors to engage in prostitution; the court imposed 18 months in jail and subsequent community control.
events.limitations: These are the historical statutory offense labels. OPR summary, printed p. ii.

events.title: Post-conviction Harvard office visits
events.summary: Harvard's review identified more than 40 visits to PED offices during 2010–2018.
events.limitations: Start of a range; Harvard could not establish the precise total.

events.title: Black retains Epstein for financial advice
events.summary: The Dechert review describes advisory work during 2012–2017 and $158 million in compensation.
events.limitations: Printed pp. 3–4. The review characterized the services as legitimate and found no evidence of criminal involvement by Black; this was a commissioned review, not a court finding.

events.title: MIT review records a campus meeting
events.summary: MIT's report places Epstein, Ito, Hoffman and Gershenfeld at a meeting; Ito said Smith joined part of the discussion.
events.limitations: Printed p. 47. Smith's participation is attributed to Ito's recollection. Attendance is not evidence of involvement in abuse.

events.title: Deutsche Bank opens Epstein-company accounts
events.summary: NYDFS records initial brokerage accounts for Southern Trust Company and Southern Financial on this date.
events.limitations: Consent-order paragraph 24; the bank ended the relationship in December 2018.

events.title: MIT donations support Bach's research
events.summary: MIT's review attributes $300,000 in November 2013 and July and September 2014 donations to support for Joscha Bach.
events.limitations: Printed p. 10. Institution-directed research funding is not evidence of criminal participation.

events.title: New York federal trafficking charges unsealed
events.summary: Prosecutors announced charges of sex trafficking of minors and conspiracy relating to alleged conduct during 2002–2005.
events.limitations: United States v. Epstein, 19 Cr. 490. Charges were allegations; the case did not reach trial.

events.title: Epstein dies in federal custody
events.summary: Epstein died while awaiting trial. New York's medical examiner ruled the death a suicide.
events.limitations: OIG later documented serious custody failures; its investigation found no evidence contradicting the FBI's determination that the death did not result from a criminal act.

events.title: Federal indictment dismissed after death
events.summary: The court dismissed the 2019 indictment following Epstein's death.
events.limitations: Procedural termination after death, not acquittal or conviction.

events.title: Ito resigns from MIT
events.summary: Joi Ito resigned after reporting on Epstein donations and visits; MIT commissioned a fact-finding review.
events.limitations: Institutional accountability event, not a criminal finding against Ito.

events.title: MIT publishes donation and visit review
events.summary: The review counted 10 Epstein donations totaling $850,000 during 2002–2017, including $750,000 after his conviction, and at least nine campus visits during 2013–2017.
events.limitations: A university-commissioned review. Its scope focused on donations, campus visits and decision-making.

events.title: MIT redirects an equivalent amount to survivor support
events.summary: MIT announced $850,000 for four nonprofits supporting survivors of sexual abuse, matching the Epstein gifts identified by its review.
events.limitations: Institutional announcement of grants; recipient and survivor personal information is not reproduced.

events.title: Harvard publishes its review
events.summary: Harvard released findings on Epstein gifts, his visiting fellowship and continued PED access after conviction.
events.limitations: Institutional review; its findings do not establish criminal involvement by faculty who met him.

events.title: NYDFS imposes Deutsche Bank penalty
events.summary: A $150 million consent-order penalty addressed compliance failures in Deutsche Bank's Epstein, Danske Estonia and FBME relationships.
events.limitations: The total penalty was not allocated solely to Epstein. Regulatory compliance findings differ from criminal convictions.

events.title: DOJ criticizes handling of the non-prosecution deal
events.summary: OPR found Acosta exercised poor judgment and victims were not treated with expected candor and sensitivity; it did not find professional misconduct by DOJ attorneys.
events.limitations: This was an internal professional-responsibility review, with a specific remit and legal standard.

events.title: Jury convicts Maxwell
events.summary: A federal jury found Maxwell guilty on five counts concerning the recruitment, transportation and trafficking of minors with Epstein.
events.limitations: She was acquitted on one tried count; the court later treated three conspiracy counts as multiplicitous for judgment.

events.title: Maxwell receives a 20-year prison sentence
events.summary: The court sentenced Maxwell to 240 months for her role in the abuse scheme.
events.limitations: United States v. Maxwell, 20 Cr. 330. Conviction and sentence are adjudicated facts.

events.title: Inspector General documents detention failures
events.summary: DOJ OIG reported serious failures in supervision, records and recording systems during Epstein's detention.
events.limitations: The report did not establish homicide; it found no evidence contradicting the FBI's conclusion about the death.

events.title: JPMorgan settles USVI civil case
events.summary: JPMorgan agreed to pay $75 million to resolve the Virgin Islands' Epstein-related civil lawsuit.
events.limitations: Case 1:22-cv-10904 (SDNY). Settlement resolved allegations without a trial; it is not a criminal conviction.

events.title: JPMorgan survivor settlement receives final approval
events.summary: JPMorgan's issuer disclosure records final approval of a $290 million settlement paid to a survivor fund.
events.limitations: Doe 1 v. JPMorgan Chase Bank, 1:22-cv-10019 (JSR). A civil settlement, not a criminal conviction.

events.title: DOJ releases first-phase records
events.summary: DOJ announced publication of records including flight logs and a redacted contact book.
events.limitations: A flight-log entry, contact-book listing or document mention does not establish participation in a crime.

events.title: DOJ and FBI publish review conclusions
events.summary: The agencies said their review found no incriminating client list or credible evidence of blackmail of prominent people.
events.limitations: Agency conclusions quoted in the court's August 11 order, p. 7. This is a dated statement about that review, not a claim that every historical allegation has been adjudicated.

events.title: DOJ announces a much larger files release
events.summary: DOJ reported nearly 3.5 million released pages in total, together with more than 2,000 videos and 180,000 images.
events.limitations: Counts are DOJ's stated production totals. DOJ warned the corpus includes potentially false public submissions. This dataset does not claim to have reviewed the whole release.

events.title: Court denies Maxwell's post-conviction petition
events.summary: Judge Paul Engelmayer denied Maxwell's section 2255 challenge, including arguments based on newly released Epstein materials.
events.limitations: Maxwell v. United States, 25 Civ. 10468 (PAE), Dkt. 10. This identifies the specific ruling, without predicting future proceedings.

coverage.title: Epstein: cases, institutions and public records
coverage.status: Selected, source-checked research; not an exhaustive archive
coverage.scope: Criminal case history; institutional reviews; AI-research donations; a specifically documented campus meeting; banking and civil settlements; public disclosure milestones.
coverage.datePrecision: YYYY or YYYY-MM values preserve the source's available precision. For ranges, the date is the beginning unless the text identifies an endpoint.
coverage.evidenceMeaning: Documented means the cited source directly records the event, relationship or attributed institutional finding. It does not convert an allegation in a document into established fact.
readingRules: A document mention, flight log, address-book entry, meeting, photograph or donation is not proof of criminal conduct.
Convictions, untried indictments, civil allegations, settlements, regulator findings and commissioned reviews are different evidence categories.
DOJ says the 2026 corpus includes potentially false submissions from members of the public; a DOJ-hosted file is not automatic authentication of its assertions.
No victim names, private contact details, addresses or graphic material are included.
Do not infer connections to intelligence agencies, countries or ethnic or religious communities from the relationships shown here.
Leon Black, Apollo Global Management, BlackRock, Blackstone and Blackwater are distinct names and organizations; similar wording is not evidence of a connection.
gaps: The full multi-million-page corpus, all correspondence, all flight entries and all claimed dinner or lunch attendees were not reviewed.
No complete or authenticated criminal 'client list' is asserted.
No Epstein–CIA, Epstein–Mossad, Epstein–BlackRock, Epstein–Blackwater or state-control edge was established by this selected research.
The dataset does not reproduce disputed sexual allegations against uncharged third parties.
The $75 million Deutsche Bank survivor settlement and additional estate or other-bank settlements require their own source and procedural-status review before addition.

Later challenges to commissioned-review conclusions and congressional inquiries should be added as separately attributed developments, with responses, rather than silently replacing the original findings.
